note: Both v6 deaths had the same cause. In each, Mario was on the ground and the jump was due by the next decision: seed 202 at t=28 with a green koopa ahead, and seed 101 at t=139 at the 3-wide pit near tile 234. The same thing happened at the seed 303 two-tile wall at t=90. Each time jev ignored the hop rule and chose run, and the extractor had assumed the jump was pressed, so on the next frame it reported S as still held (jumpKey wait) and blocked the jump that could still have saved him. Fixes: (1) when a jump expected from 'start' did not happen, the extractor now treats S as released, and only assumes S is stuck after three misses in a row; (2) a non-jump plan that needs its jump at the very next decision now has its gain counted 0.8 lower, so 'highest gain' gives the same answer as the old hop rule, and the hop field is gone; (3) the rules are now a short first-match list using a precomputed jumpEdge and plain jump triggers: no safe non-jump, stuck, wallAhead ≤ 3, pitAhead ≤ 2, or jumpEdge > 0.3. As the trainer asked, rule 5c says when to jump a wall (once it is 3 tiles or less ahead) and how (the best safe jump action, then hold S through the boost). New tests pin this on the seed 101 and 202 windows.

instructions:
Infinite Mario: get Mario as far to the right as possible without dying. The state already holds everything you need; decide only by comparing its fields as the rules below say.
FIELDS
- status: playing; none (no level on screen); dying; won.
- jumpKey: what pressing S (the jump actions jump, jumpRight, runJumpRight) does now. start = Mario is on the ground and a jump starts. landing = Mario is in the air but touches down just before the press takes effect, so the jump starts as he lands. boost = Mario is rising in a jump and holding S lifts him higher. wait = pressing S now starts nothing and only blocks the next jump.
- outcome[action]: a physics lookahead of the next 0.9 s if that action is chosen now (level, enemies and input delay are simulated; the plan may jump again later where that helps; plans that only survive with perfect timing count as failures). fate: safe; stomp (lands on an enemy, which is fine); hurt (touches an enemy, piranha or bullet: small Mario dies); pit (falls to his death). gain (given when safe or stomp): tiles of progress to the right, higher is better. When jumpKey is start or landing, a non-jump action whose plan needs its jump at the very next decision is already counted 0.8 lower, because that late jump can miss. t (given when hurt or pit): ms until the harm.
- jumpEdge: the highest gain of a safe-or-stomp jump action minus the highest gain of a safe-or-stomp non-jump action; null when either group has none or jumpKey is wait.
- wallAhead / wallHeight: tiles from Mario's front to the next solid wall at his feet, and how many tiles tall it is (null / 0 when there is none within 12 tiles). Running into a wall only stops Mario; a jump is the only way over it.
- pitAhead / pitWidth: tiles from Mario's front to the next pit (0 or less = his front is already over it) and its width (null / 0 when none).
- stuck: true when Mario has stood on the ground without moving for about 0.4 s. jumpHeld: S is still held from the last decision. big: big Mario survives one hit. threat: the nearest enemy, for information.
RULES - go down the list and apply the first rule that fits.
1. status none: choose jump or idle. status dying or won: choose idle.
2. When jumpKey is wait, jump, jumpRight and runJumpRight are not allowed. An allowed action is good when its fate is safe or stomp.
3. No allowed action is good: if big is true and an allowed action has fate hurt, choose the hurt action with the largest t; otherwise choose the allowed action with the largest t.
4. jumpKey is boost and a jump action is good: choose the good jump action with the highest gain (keep S held so the jump reaches full height).
5. jumpKey is start or landing and a jump action is good. JUMP NOW - choose the good jump action with the highest gain (runJumpRight on a tie) - when ANY of these is true:
 a) no non-jump action is good;
 b) stuck is true;
 c) a wall is close: wallAhead is not null and wallAhead is 3 or less. This is how to clear a wall: jump as soon as it is 3 tiles or less ahead, then rule 4 keeps S held while Mario rises, and the right key carries him onto the top;
 d) a pit is close: pitAhead is not null and pitAhead is 2 or less;
 e) jumpEdge is greater than 0.3.
 If none of a) to e) is true, do not jump: choose the good non-jump action (idle, left, right or run) with the highest gain (run on a tie).
6. Otherwise choose the good action with the highest gain (run on a tie).

actions.description: release every key: slow down and wait
run right with A held (fire Mario throws a fireball each time A is pressed again)
jump straight up, or keep holding jump to rise higher
jump while walking right, or keep holding jump
jump while running right, or keep holding jump
